name: Vibe Coding Studio Delivery Workflow
description: Coordinate evidence-based, platform-agnostic application delivery from authorized product idea through requirements, architecture, implementation, verification, deployment, and maintenance.
trigger: An authorized owner requests a website or application with defined users, outcome, scope, constraints, and release authority.

stages.name: Authorize product brief
stages.action: Confirm owner, users, outcome, scope, data, budget, constraints, platform assumptions, and release authority.

stages.name: Define and prioritize
stages.action: Use AA-SKL-000022, AA-SKL-000023, and AA-SKL-000031 to define acceptance criteria and the smallest valuable release.

stages.name: Design experience and architecture
stages.action: Use AA-SKL-000024 through AA-SKL-000027, AA-SKL-000033, and AA-SKL-000048; record data, identity, permissions, integration, failure, and accessibility decisions.

stages.name: Build controlled increments
stages.action: Use AA-SKL-000042 and AA-SKL-000047 plus the selected product-pattern skills; preserve versions and review generated code before acceptance.

stages.name: Verify complete behavior
stages.action: Use AA-SKL-000028, AA-SKL-000043, AA-SKL-000044, AA-SKL-000045, and AA-SKL-000046 across unit, integration, security, accessibility, failure, recovery, and end-to-end scenarios.

stages.name: Release safely
stages.action: Use AA-SKL-000029 and AA-SKL-000032 with environment separation, secrets controls, migrations, observability, rollback, approval, and release notes.

stages.name: Operate and improve
stages.action: Use AA-SKL-000030 to monitor reliability, security, cost, adoption, incidents, dependencies, and prioritized maintenance.

completion_criteria: Approved scope and acceptance criteria are traceable
Architecture and authorization match the data and risk
Critical user journeys and failure paths have evidence
Deployment, migrations, monitoring, rollback, and ownership are approved
Release status and unresolved limitations are accurate

failure_policy.escalation: Stop the affected release, preserve the last verified version and evidence, reconcile data or external effects, roll back when thresholds are met, and escalate unresolved security, privacy, integrity, cost, availability, or authority failures.
